ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.claim: Abraham’s questions expose the idols’ baselessness; the people have no answer and persist only because they follow their forefathers, a tradition they will not abandon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.anchor: because they are only following the ways of their forefathers, which they will not give up at any cost

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.claim: The reported events occur after Abraham had conclusively conveyed the truth through both scriptural and intellectual arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.anchor: when he had conclusively communicated the truth to his people through both scriptural and intellectual arguments

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r2.claim: بل وجدنا avoids the question: any direct claim about the idols’ hearing or power would expose the idolaters to an obvious lie or error, so they retreat to unsupported imitation of their fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r2.anchor: قالوا بل وجدنا هذه حيدة عن جواب الاستفهام، لأنهم لو قالوا: يسمعوننا وينفعوننا ويضروننا، فضحوا أنفسهم بالكذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r3.claim: The كاف in كذلك is an accusative object of يفعلون, referring to the same act of worshipping the idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r3.anchor: والكاف في موضع نصب بيفعلون، أي يفعلون في عبادتهم تلك الأصنام مثل ذلك الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r4.claim: Their diversion from the question signals that their argument has collapsed; بل shifts to an unrelated answer and thereby admits helplessness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r4.anchor: والحيدة عن الجواب من علامات انقطاع الحجة. وبل هنا إضراب عن جوابه لما سأل وأخذ في شيء آخر لم يسألهم عنه انقطاعا وإقرارا بالعجز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117/r1.claim: The people concede the idols neither hear nor bring benefit nor avert harm, but say they follow their fathers; this refutes religious imitation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117/r1.anchor: لكن اقتدينا بآبائنا. فيه إبطال التقليد في الدين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r4.claim: The people stop claiming the idols hear or affect them and retreat to imitation of their forefathers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r4.anchor: أضربوا عن أن يكون لهم سمع أو يتوقع منهم ضر أو نفع، والتجأوا إلى التقليد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r5.speaker: العبدة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r5.claim: The worshippers justify their practice by saying their earlier ancestors must have recognized something good in it and were wiser and more experienced.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r5.anchor: فلولا أنهم رأوا ذلك حسنان ما واظبوا عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r6.claim: People would abandon a practice that caused visible physical harm, yet religious custom has long made false imitation easy to maintain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r6.anchor: هذا الدين يهون على الناس فيه التقليد بالباطل قديما وحديثا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r10.claim: Their appeal to ancestral practice is the worst form of imitation because it defends error on a clear and momentous matter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r10.anchor: وقولهم بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون، أقبح وجوه التقليد لأنه على ضلالة وفي أمر بين خلافه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.claim: The people concede that their idols do not hear, benefit, or harm; they follow their ancestors' practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.anchor: اعترفوا بأن (1) أصنامهم لا تفعل شيئا من ذلك، وإنما رأوا آباءهم كذلك يفعلون

JISHUMI:v7p5364/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5364/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5364/r23.claim: By citing their fathers, the people admit that idols neither hear nor benefit nor harm; they follow custom rather than argument.
JISHUMI:v7p5364/r23.anchor: وبينوا أنهم سلكوا في عبادتها طريقة التقليد لا طريقة الحجاج

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.claim: They defend worship by saying they found their fathers doing it; Abraham then asks about the idols worshipped by them and their earliest ancestors.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.anchor: يعنى هكذا يعبدون الأصنام { قال } إبراهيم:

QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r12.claim: The people abandon argument and appeal to ancestral imitation without proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r12.anchor: فنزعوا إلى التقليد من غير حجة ولا دليل

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r10.claim: The people answer the proof by appealing to their ancestors; this demonstrates the error of blind imitation and the duty to use evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r10.anchor: وهذا من أقوى الدلائل على فساد التقليد ووجوب التمسك بالاستدلال

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r11.claim: If imitation were praised and reasoning condemned, one would praise the unbelievers’ condemned way and condemn Abraham’s praised way.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r11.anchor: لكان ذلك مدحا لطريقة الكفار التي ذمها الله تعالى وذما لطريقة إبراهيم عليه السلام التي مدحها الله تعالى

STUDYQURAN:26:74/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r1.claim: The idolaters concede that their idols have no power to harm or benefit them.
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r1.anchor: The idolaters admit that the idols do not have the power to harm or benefit (IK)

STUDYQURAN:26:74/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī treats reliance on inherited authority as an argument against taqlīd and for belief grounded in sound reasoning and proof.
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r2.anchor: This is, for al-Rāzī, a clear argument against belief based on conformity with authority

STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.claim: The source links this rejection of ancestral imitation to 5:104 and similar injunctions in 7:28, 10:78, 28:36, 31:21, and 43:24.
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.anchor: For the notion of idolaters blindly following the ways of their forefathers, see commentary on 5:104

TABATABAI:26:70-75/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r7.claim: Rather than answer the questions negatively and concede the idols’ impotence, Abraham’s people retreat to ancestor imitation as their only support for idolatry.
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r7.anchor: لكنه لما كان ينتج خلاف ما هم عليه من الانتحال بالوثنية أضربوا عنه إلى التشبث بذيل التقليد

TABATABAI:26:74-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r1.claim: “We found our fathers doing this” means they acted and worshiped as their fathers did; the phrasing emphasizes imitation of ritual forms without understanding anything beyond them.
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r1.anchor: ففعلنا كما كانوا يفعلون وعبدناهم كما كانوا يعبدون

TABRISI:26:72-77/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r14.claim: The people admit they follow the practice of their forefathers, exposing their reliance on inherited imitation.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r14.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن تقليدهم آباءهم في عبادة الأصنام

THALABI:v7p166/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p166/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p166/r4.claim: The passage shows that religion must rest on proof and that blind imitation is invalid in matters of faith.
THALABI:v7p166/r4.anchor: وفي هذه الآية بيان أن الدين إنما يثبت بالحجة وبطلان التقليد فيه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r7.claim: Having no argument, Abraham's people could only appeal to what their ancestors did.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r7.anchor: {قالوا بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون} [الشعراء: 74] فلم تكن لهم حجة فقالوا هذا القول وليس لهم حجة.

SAMIN-DURR:26:74/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:74/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:74/r1.claim: Kathālika is accusative, governed by yafʿalūn, with the sense they do the same as we do; yafʿalūn is the second object of wajadnā.
SAMIN-DURR:26:74/r1.anchor: يفعلون في محل نصب مفعولا ثانيا ل

ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r1.claim: The initial particle bal expresses astonishment.
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r1.anchor: The particle bal at the beginning of the sentence expresses astonishment.

ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r2.claim: Abraham's people evade his criticism of idol worship by stressing its antiquity.
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r2.anchor: evading a direct answer to Abraham's criticism of idol-worship, his people merely stress its antiquity

ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r3.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r3.claim: Zamakhshari argues that ancient usage and chronological precedence do not prove a concept sound.
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r3.anchor: Zamakhshari points out - that "ancient usage and precedence in time are no proof of [a concept's] soundness"

ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r4.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r4.claim: Razi calls the verse a powerful Qur'anic indictment of taqlid: blind adoption of religious ideas on a scholar's or leader's authority.
ASAD-NOTES:26:74#n38/r4.anchor: Razi, for his part, states that the above verse represents "one of the strongest [Qur'anic] indications

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r1.claim: They abandon any claim that their idols hear, benefit, or harm, conceding what cannot be denied; they admit that their sole warrant is imitation of their fathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r1.anchor: أضربوا عن أن يكون لهم سمع أو نفع أو ضرا اعترافا بما لاسبيل لهم إلى انكاره

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r2.claim: They mean that their fathers did the same and worshipped the idols in the same way; the absolute object is fronted to preserve the rhyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r2.anchor: وإنما وجدنا آباءنا يفعلون مثل فعلنا ويعبدونهم مثل عبادتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#3/r3.claim: The absolute object is placed first for the sake of the verse ending.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq recounts that Abraham’s father made idols for him to sell; Abraham mocked them as harmful and useless, then tipped their heads into a river and told them to drink. The ridicule spread locally but had not reached Nimrod.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال رجع إبراهيم إلى أبيه ازر وقد استقامت وجهته وعرف رده

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r1.speaker: بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r1.claim: Burayda saw people copying one another and warned that they would soon say, «We found our fathers doing the same».
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بريدة ، عن أبيه انه راى قوما يمر بعضهم على بعض فقال : يوشك هؤلاء

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r2.claim: Qatāda says they followed their forefathers’ religion and were themselves following them.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779/r2.anchor: عن قتادة يعني قوله : بل وجدنا ابائنا كذلك يفعلون يعني على دين وانا متبعوهم على ذلك

BURSEVI:v6p204/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r7.claim: كذلك is governed by يفعلون and is the second object of وجدنا.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r7.anchor: منصوب بقوله : {يفعلون} وهو مفعول ثان لوجدنا

BURSEVI:v6p204/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r8.claim: They admit the idols cannot hear, benefit, or harm, and confess they followed their fathers as their only support.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r8.anchor: وجدناهم يعبدون مثل عبادتنا فاقتدينا بهم اعترفوا بأنها بمعزل من السمع والمنفعة والمضرة

BURSEVI:v6p204/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r9.claim: The Persian couplet warns truth-seekers not to follow an imitator's path to the Kaaba.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r9.anchor: خواهي بسوى كعبه تحقيق ره برى ي بري مقلدكم كرده ره مرو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#3/r1.claim: They answer by admitting that they merely imitate their forefathers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r1.claim: Ibrahim pushes their appeal to inherited practice to its oldest ancestors: precedence proves nothing, and falsehood does not become true through age.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r1.anchor: لما أجابوه بجواب المقلدين لآبائهم قال لهم : رقوا أمر تقليدكم هذا إلى أقصى غاياته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#7/r1.claim: Their rather retracts the claim that idols hear, benefit, or harm: they worship them for none of those reasons, but imitate their ancestors.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#7/r1.anchor: إضراب أى لا تسمع ولا تنفع ولا تضر ولا نعبدها لشئ من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v17p590/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r3.claim: Their بل turns from the denied claim about the idols' powers to the actual reason for their practice, like saying, 'It was not so, but rather this.'
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r3.anchor: وذلك رجوع عن مجحود، كقول القائل: ما كان كذا بل كذا وكذا،

TAB-FULL:v17p590/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r4.claim: They say their forebears worshipped and served the idols, and they follow their ancestors' example and way.
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r4.anchor: فنحن نفعل ذلك اقتداء بهم، واتباعا لمنهاجهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65/r1.claim: They admit imitating their ancestors in idol worship and abandoning proof and reasoning, despite acknowledging that idols neither hear, harm, nor benefit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65/r1.anchor: وهذا إخبار أنهم قلدوا آباءهم في عبادة الأصنام، وتركوا الحجة والاستدلال
